answer: At dawn, agents trading juniper on a marketplace must each lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before submitting at most one offer per hour. A ripple of new identities cannot bypass that limit cheaply: 1,000 active accounts require $1 million immobilized for a month. The bond does not prove identities are unique; it makes each extra account consume scarce capital, so a sybil swarm pays in proportion to its reach.
